text: If two circles touch one another, (then) they will not have the same center. For let the two circles $ABC$ and $CDE$ touch one another at point $C$. I say that they will not have the same center.
For, if possible, let $F$ be (the common center),
assertion: F is (supposed to be) the common center

frame.supposition: point $F$ is the (common) center of the circles $ABC$ and $CDE$

text: and let $FEB$ be drawn through (the two circles), at random.
Therefore, since point $F$ is the center of the circle $ABC$, $FC$ is equal to $FB$.

spans.label: assumption
spans.text: point $F$ is the center of the circle $ABC$

text: Again, since point $F$ is the center of the circle $CDE$, $FC$ is equal to $FE$.

spans.label: assumption
spans.text: point $F$ is the center of the circle $CDE$

text: But $FC$ was shown (to be) equal to $FB$. Thus, $FE$ is also equal to $FB$, the lesser to the greater.
assertion: FE is equal to FB (the lesser to the greater)

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: $FE$ is also equal to $FB$, the lesser to the greater

text: Thus, point $F$ is not the (common) center of the circles $ABC$ and $CDE$.
assertion: point F is not the (common) center of the circles ABC and CDE

frame.closes: point $F$ is the (common) center of the circles $ABC$ and $CDE$

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: point $F$ is not the (common) center of the circles $ABC$ and $CDE$

text: Thus, if two circles touch one another, (then) they will not have the same center. (Which is) the very thing it was required to show.
